grammarTopics.title: Adverbial clauses of time, reason, purpose and concession
grammarTopics.explanation: Mit Konjunktionen verbindest du Haupt- und Nebensatz logisch. Zeit: after (nachdem), as soon as (sobald), before (bevor), until (bis), when (wenn/als), whenever (jedes Mal, wenn), while (während). Grund: because (weil). Zweck: so that (damit). Einräumung: although (obwohl). Komma: Nebensatz zuerst → Komma; Hauptsatz zuerst → kein Komma.
examples: After I spoke to my friend, I felt much better.
Things often get better as soon as you talk to somebody.
Carol wrote to an agony aunt because she had a problem.
Write to Ruby so that she can give you advice.
They had a big fight although they were best friends.
commonMistakes: so that und because verwechseln (Zweck ↔ Grund)
Komma, obwohl der Hauptsatz zuerst steht

grammarTopics.title: Modals and their substitute forms (be allowed to, be able to, have to)
grammarTopics.explanation: can, may, must, mustn't, needn't gibt es nur im simple present. Für andere Zeitformen brauchst du Ersatzformen: Erlaubnis/Verbot → be allowed to (was/weren't allowed to), Fähigkeit → be able to (was able to), Notwendigkeit → have to (had to, didn't have to). Achtung: mustn't = darf nicht; needn't / don't have to = muss nicht.
examples: Olivia is allowed to use her parents' computer.
She was allowed to play a game on it last weekend.
When I was young, I wasn't able to look everything up on the internet.
He had to ask somebody for help.
We didn't have to wait long.
commonMistakes: „musted" oder „must" für die Vergangenheit statt „had to"
mustn't (darf nicht) mit needn't (muss nicht) verwechseln
Form von be vergessen: „I allowed to …"

grammarTopics.title: should, shouldn't, could
grammarTopics.explanation: Mit should (solltest), shouldn't (solltest nicht) und could (könntest) machst du Vorschläge und gibst Ratschläge. Wie alle Modalverben sind sie in allen Personen gleich (kein -s), und danach steht das Vollverb in der Grundform ohne to.
examples: Mr Elliot could look for help on the internet.
They should ask their parents for advice.
You shouldn't try to fix everything yourself.
You could look at a forum for help. But you shouldn't believe everything you read online.
commonMistakes: to nach dem Modalverb: „You should to ask …"
-s beim Modalverb oder Vollverb: „She shoulds …", „He could looks …"

grammarQuestions.prompt: ___ I spoke to my friend, I felt much better.
grammarQuestions.explanation: Zeitliche Reihenfolge: nachdem → after.

optionHints.Although: although = obwohl – das passt hier nicht.
optionHints.So that: so that = damit (Zweck) – hier geht es um die zeitliche Reihenfolge.

grammarQuestions.prompt: Carol wrote to an agony aunt ___ she had a problem.
grammarQuestions.explanation: Grund: weil sie ein Problem hatte → because.

optionHints.although: although = obwohl. Hier ist es ein Grund → because.
optionHints.so that: so that = damit. Hier ist es ein Grund → because.

grammarQuestions.prompt: Write to Ruby ___ she can give you advice.
grammarQuestions.explanation: Zweck: damit sie dir Rat geben kann → so that.

optionHints.because: because = weil. Hier geht es um einen Zweck → so that.

grammarQuestions.prompt: They had a big fight ___ they were best friends.
grammarQuestions.explanation: Gegensatz: obwohl sie beste Freundinnen waren → although.

optionHints.because: Sie stritten nicht, WEIL sie Freundinnen waren – es ist ein Gegensatz.
optionHints.so that: so that = damit – passt hier nicht.

grammarQuestions.prompt: Things often get better ___ you talk to somebody.
grammarQuestions.explanation: as soon as = sobald.

optionHints.until: until = bis – der Sinn wäre falsch.

grammarQuestions.prompt: Never give out your address ___ you've really met your new friend.
grammarQuestions.explanation: until = bis (erst wenn).

optionHints.because: because = weil – der Sinn wäre falsch.

grammarQuestions.explanation: Grund → because.

grammarQuestions.explanation: as soon as = sobald.

grammarQuestions.prompt: When I was young, I ___ look everything up on the internet.
grammarQuestions.explanation: Fähigkeit in der Vergangenheit → was/wasn't able to.

optionHints.can't: can gibt es nur im simple present. Vergangenheit: wasn't able to.
optionHints.didn't able to: be able to wird mit be verneint: wasn't able to.

grammarQuestions.prompt: Olivia ___ use her parents' computer. (darf)
grammarQuestions.explanation: Erlaubnis → be allowed to.

optionHints.is able to: be able to = können (Fähigkeit). Erlaubnis: be allowed to.
optionHints.has to: have to = müssen. Erlaubnis: be allowed to.

grammarQuestions.prompt: She ___ play a game on it last weekend. (durfte)
grammarQuestions.explanation: Erlaubnis in der Vergangenheit → was allowed to.

optionHints.is allowed to: last weekend → Vergangenheit: was allowed to.
optionHints.had allowed to: Die Ersatzform heißt be allowed to → was allowed to.

grammarQuestions.prompt: Mrs Elliot ___ do the shopping yesterday. (musste)
grammarQuestions.explanation: must gibt es nur im simple present. Vergangenheit: had to.

optionHints.must: must hat keine Vergangenheitsform – du brauchst had to.

grammarQuestions.prompt: You ___ look for the phone number. I've got it. (musst nicht)
grammarQuestions.explanation: muss nicht = don't have to (oder needn't).

optionHints.mustn't: Vorsicht: mustn't = darfst nicht! Muss nicht = don't have to / needn't.
optionHints.aren't allowed to: aren't allowed to = darfst nicht. Muss nicht = don't have to.

grammarQuestions.prompt: In my last school we ___ use computers just for fun. (durften nicht)
grammarQuestions.explanation: Verbot in der Vergangenheit → weren't allowed to.

optionHints.didn't have to: didn't have to = mussten nicht. Verbot: weren't allowed to.
optionHints.weren't able to: weren't able to = konnten nicht. Verbot: weren't allowed to.

grammarQuestions.prompt: We ___ wait long. The bus came quickly. (mussten nicht)
grammarQuestions.explanation: mussten nicht → didn't have to.

optionHints.mustn't: mustn't = darf nicht, und nur Gegenwart. Mussten nicht: didn't have to.
optionHints.weren't allowed to: Das hieße „durften nicht warten". Gemeint: mussten nicht → didn't have to.

grammarQuestions.prompt: Luke ___ help his dad with the washing machine. (kann – Ersatzform)
grammarQuestions.explanation: Fähigkeit, simple present → is able to.

grammarQuestions.prompt: When the boys were four, they ___ swim. (konnten nicht – Ersatzform)
grammarQuestions.explanation: Fähigkeit in der Vergangenheit, verneint → weren't able to.

grammarQuestions.prompt: He ___ ask somebody for help. (musste)
grammarQuestions.explanation: Notwendigkeit in der Vergangenheit → had to.

grammarQuestions.prompt: ___ I allowed to use your tablet, Dad?
grammarQuestions.explanation: Frage mit be allowed to: Am I allowed to …?

grammarQuestions.prompt: Mr Elliot ___ work in the evenings. (muss nicht)
grammarQuestions.explanation: muss nicht → doesn't have to (oder needn't).

grammarQuestions.prompt: ___ you allowed to use your dad's tablet when you were younger?
grammarQuestions.explanation: Frage in der Vergangenheit mit be allowed to: Were you allowed to …?

grammarQuestions.prompt: You ___ believe everything you read online.
grammarQuestions.explanation: Rat, etwas NICHT zu tun → shouldn't.

optionHints.should: Man sollte nicht alles glauben → shouldn't.
optionHints.could: could ist ein Vorschlag („könntest") – hier ist eine Warnung gemeint → shouldn't.

grammarQuestions.prompt: They ___ ask their parents for advice. (sollten)
grammarQuestions.explanation: Ratschlag: sie sollten → should.

optionHints.shouldn't: shouldn't = sollten nicht. Gemeint: sollten → should.
optionHints.must not: must not = dürfen nicht. Gemeint: sollten → should.

grammarQuestions.prompt: Mr Elliot could ___ for help on the internet.
grammarQuestions.explanation: Nach Modalverben steht die Grundform ohne to.

optionHints.looks: Nach could steht die Grundform – kein -s.
optionHints.to look: Nach Modalverben kein to: could look.

grammarQuestions.prompt: Herr Elliot könnte im Internet nach Hilfe suchen. =

Mr Elliot coulds look for help on the internet.
grammarQuestions.answer: Mr Elliot could look for help on the internet.
grammarQuestions.explanation: could + Grundform: could look.

optionHints.Mr Elliot could looking for help on the: Nach could kommt die Grundform, kein -ing.

grammarQuestions.prompt: I've got a headache. – You ___ drink some water. That always helps.
grammarQuestions.explanation: Vorschlag → could (oder should).

optionHints.shouldn't: Wasser trinken ist ein guter Vorschlag → could/should.

grammarQuestions.prompt: Du solltest nicht versuchen, alles selbst zu reparieren. =
options: You shouldn't try to fix everything yourself.
You don't should try to fix everything yourself.
You shouldn't to try to fix everything yourself.
grammarQuestions.answer: You shouldn't try to fix everything yourself.
grammarQuestions.explanation: shouldn't + Grundform.

optionHints.You don't should try to fix everything y: Modalverben verneinst du mit not: shouldn't, nicht mit don't.
optionHints.You shouldn't to try to fix everything y: Nach shouldn't kein to: shouldn't try.

grammarQuestions.prompt: She ___ play video games all night. She has a test tomorrow!
grammarQuestions.explanation: Rat, etwas nicht zu tun → shouldn't.

optionHints.should: Vor einem Test ist das keine gute Idee → shouldn't.
optionHints.could: Hier ist eine Warnung gemeint → shouldn't.

grammarQuestions.prompt: Olivia hurt a girl in netball. She ___ say sorry. (Rat)
grammarQuestions.explanation: Ratschlag → should (oder could).

grammarQuestions.prompt: Jay ruined Dave's book. He ___ buy him a new one.
grammarQuestions.explanation: Ratschlag → should (oder could).

grammarQuestions.prompt: You ___ eat so many sweets. (Rat: lieber nicht)
grammarQuestions.explanation: Rat, etwas nicht zu tun → shouldn't.

grammarQuestions.prompt: This phone doesn't work. – You ___ ask Luke. He's good at fixing things.
grammarQuestions.explanation: Vorschlag → could (oder should).

grammarQuestions.prompt: Holly's cat hides under the bed. Holly ___ be loud. (Rat: nicht)
grammarQuestions.explanation: Rat, etwas nicht zu tun → shouldn't.

grammarQuestions.prompt: Why don't you ___ (ask) your teacher?
grammarQuestions.explanation: Why don't you + Grundform …? = Warum … du nicht …? (Vorschlag)

conversationScenarios.title: Dear Ruby – Kummerkasten
conversationScenarios.goal: Ratschläge (should, could, Why don't you …?), Ersatzformen (G12–G14)
conversationScenarios.situation: Du bist die Kummerkastentante „Ruby". Lauren schreibt dir mit einem Problem.
conversationScenarios.openingLine: Dear Ruby, I'm writing to you because I don't know what to do. My parents say I'm not allowed to use my phone after 8 p.m. …

n1.npcLine: Dear Ruby, I'm writing to you because I don't know what to do. My parents say I'm not allowed to use my phone after 8 p.m. All my friends are allowed to chat until 10. What should I do? – Lauren

choices.text: Dear Lauren, I'm sorry you're feeling sad. My advice is to talk to your parents.
choices.feedback: Einfühlsam und ein klarer Rat – wie eine echte Kummerkastentante!
Guter Rat! Etwas freundlicher: Dear Lauren, my advice is to talk to your parents.

choices.text: You should to talk to your parents.
choices.feedback: Nach should kein to: You should talk to your parents.

n2.npcLine: But I've already talked to them! They say I have to do my homework first.

choices.text: Why don't you do your homework as soon as you get home? Then you could chat a bit before 8.
choices.feedback: Super – Why don't you …?, as soon as und could!
Okay! Mit Begründung überzeugt es mehr: Do your homework first so that you have time to chat.
mustn't = darfst nicht – das wäre ein schlechter Rat! Besser: You should do your homework first.

n3.npcLine: OK, that's a good idea. But what about my friends? They chat in the evening and I feel left out.

choices.text: You could ask your friends to chat a bit earlier. Real friends will understand.
choices.feedback: Ein freundlicher, kluger Vorschlag mit could.
Ein Anfang! Genauer: You could tell your friends about the rule.

choices.text: You should chat although your parents say no.
choices.feedback: Das bringt nur Ärger. Besser: You could ask your friends to chat earlier.

n4.npcLine: Thanks, Ruby! When I was younger, I wasn't allowed to have a phone at all. Do you think my parents will change the rule one day?

choices.text: Maybe! Show them that you can do your homework first. I hope this advice helps!

choices.feedback: Ehrlich – aber mach Lauren Mut: Maybe! I hope this advice helps.
had to = mussten (Vergangenheit). Hier passt: Maybe they will change it.

n5.npcLine: Thank you so much, Ruby. I'm going to talk to my parents tonight! – Lauren
